content: 1. Zotinib: Zotinib affects the metabolism of CYP3A4 enzymes in the liver and intestines. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering. 2. Crizotinib and Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate: Both drugs increase the QTc interval, which can lead to serious cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely if no alternative is available. 3. Crofelermer: Crofelermer increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Crofelermer may also inhibit MRP2 and OATP1A2 transporters in the gut but is unlikely to have systemic effects due to minimal absorption. 4. Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The interaction is considered minor, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 5. Cyclosporine: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Cyclosporine also increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Plasma concentrations of organic anion transporter protein substrates may also increase. 6. Dabigatran: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration if creatinine clearance (CrCl) is <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. Monitor closely. 7. Dabrafenib: Dabrafenib decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 8. Dactinomycin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dactinomycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Dalteparin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the effects of dalteparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 10. Danazol: Danazol increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Danicopan: Danicopan increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Danicopan also increases plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates, necessitating dose reductions for drugs where small concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. 12. Dapsone: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dapsone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Daridorexant: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases daridorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. The daridorexant dose should not exceed 25 mg per night when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Darifenacin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases darifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and darifenacin increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels through the same mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 15. Darunavir: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels through the same mechanism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Dasatinib: Both dasatinib and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval, posing a risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate also increases dasatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 17. Daunorubicin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases daunorubicin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Deferasirox: Deferasirox decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Deflazacort: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases deflazacort levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 20. Degarelix: Both degarelix and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs.
